blocks.text:
# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — deterministic repro of the incident: a bash call that blocks forever (sleep-forever fixture / hung `git fetch` shaped) with no declared timeout → at the 300 s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within the recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; **the same turn continues** with job id + log path, in interactive mode. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…

- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — deterministic repro of the incident: a bash call that blocks forever (sleep-forever fixture / hung `git fetch` shaped) with no declared timeout → at the 300 s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within the recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; **the same turn continues** with job id + log path, in interactive mode. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it

- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions

- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it

- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +

- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan

- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue

There it is — the root cause for the incident. The observed failure was an **interactive** session (dmtools factory session — actually, hmm, "factory session" — the user poked it with "как дела?", so it was interactive-ish; the steering came from the owner typing into it). The `effectiveStuckTool()` gate defaults interactive sessions to `advisory` — meaning at the stuck threshold only the advisory event was emitted, and nothing else happened. That's exactly what the ledger shows: `tool_stuck` at 17:10:52, heartbeats continuing every minute (the attempt never got cancelled), and no cancel/retry/convert for 22 minutes until the user's steering soft-yielded the call.

Now the goal ticket (gh-1632) says:

- **I1**: on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.

# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/

blocks.text:
# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

There it is — the root cause for the incident. The observed failure was an **interactive** session (dmtools factory session — actually, hmm, "factory session" — the user poked it with "как дела?", so it was interactive-ish; the steering came from the owner typing into it). The `effectiveStuckTool()` gate defaults interactive sessions to `advisory` — meaning at the stuck threshold only the advisory event was emitted, and nothing else happened. That's exactly what the ledger shows: `tool_stuck` at 17:10:52, heartbeats continuing every minute (the attempt never got cancelled), and no cancel/retry/convert for 22 minutes until the user's steering soft-yielded the call.

Now the goal ticket (gh-1632) says:

- **I1**: on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.

So the minimal, root-cause fix is: change `effectiveStuckTool()` so that when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` config exists, BOTH headless and interactive get the autonomous default. `advisory` remains available only via explicit config.

But wait — the ticket is a GOAL ticket with a big capability surface (recovery budget, nudge at conversion time, escalation record, ledger REG, fa version in session header, etc.). As a bug-development agent I should do the minimum targeted fix for the root cause. Let me re-read the ACs:

- AC1 — deterministic repro: bash call blocks forever, no declared timeout → at 300s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; same turn continues with job id + log path, **in interactive mode**. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- AC2 — model-facing nudge delivered at conversion time — the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result.
- AC3 — advisory mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery. UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- AC4 — recovery-budget overrun produces escalation record.
- AC5 — ledger REG: fixture session asserts tool_stuck ⇒ follow-up record within budget; CI job.
- AC6 — session header carries the fa version.
- AC7 — no false-positive regressions: declared-15-min call running 6 min NOT stuck.

# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — deterministic repro of the incident: a bash call that blocks forever (sleep-forever fixture / hung `git fetch` shaped) with no declared timeout → at the 300 s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within the recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; **the same turn continues** with job id + log path, in interactive mode. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…

  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**

| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary

  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,

  on every new user

  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe

  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe

There it is — the root cause for the incident. The observed failure was an **interactive** session (dmtools factory session — actually, hmm, "factory session" — the user poked it with "как дела?", so it was interactive-ish; the steering came from the owner typing into it). The `effectiveStuckTool()` gate defaults interactive sessions to `advisory` — meaning at the stuck threshold only the advisory event was emitted, and nothing else happened. That's exactly what the ledger shows: `tool_stuck` at 17:10:52, heartbeats continuing every minute (the attempt never got cancelled), and no cancel/retry/convert for 22 minutes until the user's steering soft-yielded the call.

Now the goal ticket (gh-1632) says:

- **I1**: on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.

So the minimal, root-cause fix is: change `effectiveStuckTool()` so that when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` config exists, BOTH headless and interactive get the autonomous default. `advisory` remains available only via explicit config.

But wait — the ticket is a GOAL ticket with a big capability surface (recovery budget, nudge at conversion time, escalation record, ledger REG, fa version in session header, etc.). As a bug-development agent I should do the minimum targeted fix for the root cause. Let me re-read the ACs:

- AC1 — deterministic repro: bash call blocks forever, no declared timeout → at 300s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; same turn continues with job id + log path, **in interactive mode**. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- AC2 — model-facing nudge delivered at conversion time — the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result.
- AC3 — advisory mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery. UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- AC4 — recovery-budget overrun produces escalation record.
- AC5 — ledger REG: fixture session asserts tool_stuck ⇒ follow-up record within budget; CI job.

# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files

The observed failure was an **interactive** session (dmtools factory session — actually, hmm, "factory session" — the user poked it with "как дела?", so it was interactive-ish; the steering came from the owner typing into it). The `effectiveStuckTool()` gate defaults interactive sessions to `advisory` — meaning at the stuck threshold only the advisory event was emitted, and nothing else happened. That's exactly what the ledger shows: `tool_stuck` at 17:10:52, heartbeats continuing every minute (the attempt never got cancelled), and no cancel/retry/convert for 22 minutes until the user's steering soft-yielded the call.

Now the goal ticket (gh-1632) says:

- **I1**: on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.

So the minimal, root-cause fix is: change `effectiveStuckTool()` so that when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` config exists, BOTH headless and interactive get the autonomous default. `advisory` remains available only via explicit config.

# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).

Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…
