{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A stuck foreground tool call in an interactive (REPL/TUI) session is never
escalated — the `tool_stuck` flag fires but the autonomous cancel → retry →
background-convert follow-up never runs, so the call hangs until a human pokes the
session (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa 1.0.580: 27 minutes hung
on a dead `git fetch`).

**Root cause**: `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` in
`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart:966-975` — when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:`
config exists, it returns `StuckToolConfig(followUp: StuckFollowUpMode.advisory)`
for every non-headless (`headlessRun == false`) host. Interactive sessions therefore
run the gh-1054 supervision in **advisory** mode by an *implicit* default, and
`_fireStuckThreshold` (agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart:484) stops at the advisory
notice: nothing is cancelled, retried, or converted. This is exactly invariant I1's
violation ("`advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out, never as an implicit
default for interactive sessions").

**Evidence** (answers the ticket's open question 1 — config default, not version
cutoff, not a broken state machine):
- The incident ledger shows `tool_stuck` at 17:10:52 followed by `tool_heartbeat`
  records continuing every minute for 22 more minutes. In autonomous mode the
  attempt is abandoned at the threshold within `cancelGrace` (10 s default) and
  heartbeats stop; only advisory mode produces "stuck flag fired, then nothing but
  heartbeats".
- The state machine itself is intact and fully tested:
  `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart` covers the full autonomous arc (threshold
  cancel → marked retry → background-convert with the turn continuing, plus the
  escalation and advisory branches); `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` runs
  the AC1/AC4/AC5 session-level parity. fa 1.0.580 shipped the machine — it was
  gated off by the interactive advisory default.
- Two tests actively pinned the buggy behavior:
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` ("the effective supervision is advisory for
  interactive hosts…") and `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` ("the interactive
  host defaults to advisory supervision…") — both cite the gh-1054 review's
  "auto-cancelling under a present human is the ticket's non-goal" stance, which
  gh-1632 supersedes.

**Impact**: Any interactive session (REPL/TUI — the default `fa` invocation) with a
wedged foreground call (hung `git fetch`, credential prompt with no tty, network
freeze) is dead until inbound user steering soft-yields the call. Headless runs are
unaffected. The deadlock is I3-shaped: the recovery nudge would queue behind a turn
that never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call needing recovery.

**Fix approach**: Make the escalation unconditional (I1) — `effectiveStuckTool()`
returns the autonomous default (`StuckToolConfig()`, `followUp: autonomous`) in
every mode when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` section is configured; `advisory`
remains reachable ONLY via explicit config (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`).
The recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 design (cancel grace + one retry with
full threshold re-arm, then one background conversion, then a session-visible
escalation) — the ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap is sketched as an owner default and
remains out of scope for this fix.

**Adjacent gap (observed, out of scope)**: the desktop-app wiring
(`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1466` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed
config, so an unconfigured app gets `null` — no supervision at all (not even
advisory). That host never emits `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated there
literally; wiring an autonomous default into the app host is a separate change.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1632.
"}

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced
  `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` onto every non-headless host when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine itself is intact —
  the incident session ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits the
  `tool_stuck` flag and never cancels/retries/converts. That is why fa 1.0.580 sat 27
  minutes on a dead `git fetch`: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then heartbeats only, until the
  owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Evidence: heartbeats continuing past the
  threshold is the advisory-only signature (autonomous mode abandons the attempt within
  `cancelGrace`); the full autonomous arc is pinned by `test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`.
- Violated the ticket's invariant I1: `advisory` must be an explicit opt-out, never an
  implicit default for interactive sessions.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous
  default (`StuckToolConfig()`) in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` config still wins, so `followUp: advisory` remains a deliberate
  opt-out. Config persistence is unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (failed before the fix, pass after):
  - `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the autonomous default applies in
    EVERY mode — advisory only via explicit config" (expected `autonomous`, got
    `advisory` on the pre-fix code).
  - `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` — "gh-1632 I1: the wired supervision is
    autonomous in EVERY mode by default" (same assertion through the wired `AgentCli`).
- Full suite: `dart test` — see CI run on this PR for the final tally; the four directly
  affected files (`test/agent/stuck_tool_test.dart`, `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/config/config_service_test.dart`) pass 243/243.

### Notes

- Behavioral change: default-config interactive (REPL/TUI) sessions now auto-cancel a
  call stuck past its threshold, retry it once, and convert the retry to a background job
  instead of flagging and waiting. Owners who want the old flag-only behavior set
  `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory` explicitly.
- No false-positive risk change: thresholds are untouched (300 s floor; `factor ×
  declared` for declared-timeout bash calls), so a declared-15-min `flutter test` running
  6 minutes is still not stuck (AC7).
- Adjacent gap observed, not changed here: the desktop-app wiring
  (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` → `AgentWiringSpec.stuckTool`) passes the raw parsed section, so
  an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all (not even advisory). It never emits
  `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
- Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape (cancel grace + one retry with full
  threshold re-arm, one background conversion, then a session-visible escalation); the
  ticket's 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner's follow-up.
